title: Low-Cal Spicy Cajun Beans
subtitle: with Brown Rice, Grilled Capsicum and Avo
description: Think eating light means eating boring? Not in our book! Our low-cal recipes have all the punchy flavour and excitement you’d expect from us, with less than 599 calories per serve.

steps.text: Prep ingredients: Check your avocado is ripe before starting this recipe (see Kitchen hack). Fill a medium saucepan three-quarters full with water and bring to the boil. Add the rice and cook for 25-27 mins until tender. Drain. Crush or finely chop the garlic. Pick the coriander leaves and finely chop the stems. Drain and rinse the beans.

Grill capsicum: While the rice is cooking, preheat the grill to high. Line an oven tray with foil. Quarter the capsicum, discarding the seeds. Put on the lined tray, skin-side up. Grill for 10-12 mins until the skin is slightly blackened. Cover and stand for 5 mins to allow the skin to steam and loosen. Remove the skin.

Cook Cajun beans: Meanwhile, heat 1 tsp olive oil in a medium saucepan over medium heat. Cook garlic, stirring, for 30 secs or until fragrant. Stir in half the tomato paste and cook for 1 min. Stir in the coriander stems, beans, tomatoes, Cajun seasoning and 1 tsp sugar and bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low and cook, covered, for 8 mins to develop the flavour. Remove from heat.

Make salsa: Cut the avocado and capsicum into 1cm chunks. Combine 2 tsp red wine vinegar and 2 tsp olive oil in a large bowl. Add the avocado, capsicum and coriander leaves to the dressing and toss to combine. Taste, then season with salt and pepper.
Serve up: Taste the beans, then season with salt and pepper. Divide the rice, Cajun beans and salsa among bowls and enjoy!

Kitchen hack: To speed up the ripening process, put the avocado in a paper bag and loosely close, then leave on the kitchen bench for a day or two. Add a banana to the bag to make the avocado ripen faster. ~ Want to take things to the next level of yum? Scatter some grated vegan cheese over the beans.
